# Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP — Adoption Playbook

> A documentation-first knowledge base for migrating to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP and for the
> design, build, and operations work that follows. Content is organized on two axes: a lifecycle
> axis (assess → design → migrate → build → operate → optimize) and a topic axis (data protection,
> data utilization, security and governance, performance, cost, multiprotocol identity).
> Findings from field technical-support work are included as anonymized reference material.

## How to read this repository

Every knowledge file under a `notes/` directory carries YAML frontmatter with an `evidence` field.
Treat it as the confidence signal:

- `verified` — reproduced by the author in the environment stated inline; `verified_on` gives the date.
- `documented` — stated in vendor or AWS documentation; `source` gives the URL.
- `field-observation` — observed once, not reproduced. Not a general rule.
- `hypothesis` — reasoned expectation, untested.

Do not present `field-observation` or `hypothesis` content as established fact. Numbers are only
meaningful together with the ONTAP version, region, and configuration stated next to them.
Naming convention used throughout: "Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP" on first mention, "FSx for ONTAP"
thereafter.

## Entry points

- [README (Japanese)](README.md): Primary hub with the two-axis navigation.
- [README (English)](README.en.md): English hub, same structure.
- [Navigation guide](docs/en/navigation.md): How to pick an entry point for your question.
- [Evidence policy](docs/en/evidence-policy.md): Definition of the four evidence tiers and what each requires.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Conventions, prohibitions, and verification steps for coding agents.

## Lifecycle playbooks

- [01 Assess](playbooks/01-assess/): Inventory of the current NAS and identification of migration constraints.
- [02 Design](playbooks/02-design/): Capacity, throughput, protocol, and protection scheme selection.
- [03 Migrate](playbooks/03-migrate/): Method selection, cutover sequencing, and rollback.
- [04 Build](playbooks/04-build/): Infrastructure as code, automation, reproducible builds.
- [05 Operate](playbooks/05-operate/): Monitoring, capacity management, incident response, change management.
- [06 Optimize](playbooks/06-optimize/): Performance and cost tuning after steady state.

## Topic domains

- [Data protection](domains/data-protection/): Snapshot, SnapMirror, SnapLock, backup and ransomware readiness.
- [Data utilization](domains/data-utilization/): Analytics, AI and RAG, access over the S3 API.
- [Security and governance](domains/security-governance/): Encryption, audit, permission design, regulated workload considerations.
- [Performance](domains/performance/): Throughput design, latency, caching, shared bandwidth behavior.
- [Cost](domains/cost/): Capacity, tiering, and the gap between estimates and measurements.
- [Multiprotocol identity](domains/multiprotocol-identity/): NFS and SMB coexistence, Active Directory integration, ID mapping.

## Reference

- [Decision trees](reference/decision-trees/): Selection flowcharts for migration method, protection scheme, and protocol.
- [Comparison matrices](reference/comparison/): Option comparisons with trade-offs stated symmetrically for every option.
- [Limits and quotas](reference/limits/): Limit values with source and verification date.
- [Glossary](reference/glossary/): ONTAP and AWS terminology.

## Case studies

- [Case studies](case-studies/): Generalized lessons from field work. Contains no company names,
  no real identifiers, and no configurations that could identify an organization.
